original.prompt: Consider the following statements about US trade measures affecting India in early 2026:
items: The White House used Section 122 of the Trade Act to impose a temporary 15% global tariff that expires in late July 2026.
Tariffs under Section 301 rest on presidential discretion rather than on formal investigations.
The India–US framework for an interim trade deal, reached in February 2026, set an 18% baseline tariff on Indian goods.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Section 301 builds on formal investigations and findings of unfair trade practices, not presidential discretion, which gives its levies a stronger legal footing. Section 301 could override the 18% baseline with higher, sector-specific duties.
original.source: It builds on formal investigations and findings of unfair trade practices rather than presidential discretion, giving any resulting levies a stronger legal foundation.
